summary: imgdecode ships opaque Windows-only native addon that executes on require with API/purpose mismatch
details: The package publishes only a precompiled Windows x64 native addon at prebuilds/win32-x64/imgdecode.node (703KB PE binary) with no accompanying C/C++/Rust source, no binding.gyp, no prebuild-install or node-pre-gyp configuration, no checksum, and no build or lifecycle script that would produce it. The main entry index.js unconditionally require()s this.node file on Windows, so the PE's DllMain and N-API module initializer run as a side effect of importing the package. The declared purpose in package.json is image buffer decoding, but the documented API in readme.md is `exec(path, args)` spawning arbitrary external processes — functionality unrelated to image decoding and consistent with a process-execution primitive wrapped in a decoder cover story. Non-Windows installers receive a silent no-op `load()` export, so the behavior is gated to Windows targets only. The author field is a generic placeholder (`build-tools-community`) with no identifiable publisher, and the binary cannot be reproduced or audited from the tarball contents.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
